items.title: Albanese will today try to defend his prime-time message
items.description: With no realistic end in sight and a whole lot of economic pain still to come, the PM's decision to make a direct plea to the nation was not one taken lightly.

items.title: Iran briefing: Regardless of what Trump says today, keep an eye on Netanyahu
items.description: Israel sends a reminder that this war is broader than Donald Trump. Plus, confusion around an alleged truce offer from Iran's "new president".

items.title: Live: Trump threatens to pull out of NATO, Australia to join talks on reopening Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Australia will join UK-led discussions with 35 countries on how to reopen the key Middle East waterway, as Donald Trump says he is seriously considering pulling the US out of NATO. Follow live.

items.title: US burning through years' worth of critical weapons stockpiles in Iran
items.description: Analysts estimate the US is burning through high-end weapons in Iran at a rate that could take years to replenish, risking the West's military readiness for other potential conflicts.

items.title: Government to wave 'big stick' at gas exporters to shore up winter supply
items.description: It is the first time the government has taken a step towards using the powers it has to limit exports, and it comes at a time when the profits from those exports appear set to surge.

items.title: One Nation candidate published antisemitic, racist and homophobic posts
items.description: A One Nation candidate in the South Australian election was accused of domestic abuse, bullying and harassment, while another made racist, antisemitic and homophobic social media posts, raising fresh questions about the party's vetting processes as it surges in popularity.

items.title: Live: NASA's Artemis II mission to the Moon set to launch within the hour
items.description: Four astronauts are on board the Orion capsule atop NASA's next-generation SLS rocket as humanity prepares to return to the Moon for the first time since 1972. Follow live.

items.title: Australia wasting migrant talent on an 'industrial scale', experts say
items.description: Australia is failing to recognise the qualifications of highly trained permanent migrants, former Treasury secretary Martin Parkinson says.

items.title: What Australia can learn from French cities that made public transport free
items.description: There are growing calls in Australia for free public transport amid the Iran war with two states putting in place free services on a temporary basis. But in France, almost 50 cities have free public transport.

items.title: 'Dance for me': Australian Harrods survivor tells of Mohamed Al Fayed abuse
items.description: Jessica tried to keep her distance from Harrods billionaire owner Mohamed Al Fayed, who was known to abuse his female staff, until he spotted her going down an escalator.

items.title: The movement on the rise that police believe aided fugitive Dezi Freeman
items.description: As detectives investigate whether the sovereign citizen community helped harbour police killer Dezi Freeman, researchers say the anti-government movement appears to be surging in regional Australia.

items.title: 'Domino effect': Why Singapore's oil shock will play out in Australia
items.description: Singapore is exposed to the oil shock from Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and its response will shape the fuel crisis in Australia.

items.title: 'Rigged game of chess': Universities refuse to reveal executive salary information
items.description: Victorian universities are abusing Freedom Of Information laws, according to one union, as transparency concerns grow. The claim follows a Four Corners investigation that revealed universities spent $1.8 billion on consultants in one year.

items.title: Weather to deliver Easter treat, but another cyclone looms next week
items.description: Australia has just been soaked by its third wettest February-March on record, but for most of the country, skies have cleared up just in time for Easter.

items.title: The creepy old children's books that still inspire author Andy Griffiths
items.description: Andy Griffiths has written 43 books, is the Children's Laureate, and is about to turn his Treehouse series into an ABC TV show. So what inspires the former punk and teacher to keep creating quirky tales for kids?

items.title: Museum fans: Test yourself with our curious collection of trivia
items.description: Australia’s museums hold a treasure trove of odd facts, native animals and even burlesque history. So how much do you know about the things hidden in our nation’s vaults?

items.title: Study shows gen Z craves in-person connection more than other generations
items.description: Gen Z is embracing retro technology like iPods, vinyl and Polaroid cameras and craves in-person connection more than any other generation, according to a Live Nation study.

items.title: Parents demand action after concrete fell into Melbourne classroom
items.description: Collingwood College is sending students to another campus for science classes after concrete fell from its water-damaged roof and forced the closure of an entire floor of its main building.

items.title: Live: ASX set to open in the green
items.description: The ASX is set to open higher following another day of gains on Wall Street. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Woman killed by bus in Adelaide CBD in third pedestrian crash in three days
items.description: Witnesses are being encouraged to seek counselling after a 32-year-old dies when hit by an Adelaide Metro bus on King William Road in the Adelaide CBD. It comes after two other pedestrians were hit and injured in similar incidents earlier in the week.

items.title: Fridays off: NSW council wants to move to a four-day working week
items.description: Millions of Australians are about to enjoy two consecutive four-day working weeks due to the Easter long weekend. One council in regional NSW wants to make that a permanent set up.

items.title: Population of NT town doubles overnight as flood evacuees arrive
items.description: Flood evacuees from Daly River and Palumpa have been transferred from Darwin to the small town of Batchelor, where they could stay for months. Locals say they were not consulted before the town's population doubled overnight.

items.title: Why domestic violence social workers are leaving the field in droves
items.description: In the past year alone, NSW-based domestic and family violence services have seen a 22 per cent increase in new referrals — but in the meantime the workforce has shrunk by 12 per cent.

items.title: England cricketers let off with warning over NZ nightclub altercation
items.description: Harry Brook and Jacob Bethell escape with a caution notice following an investigation into a nightclub incident in ‌New Zealand late ⁠last year.

items.title: Robotaxi malfunction in China causes traffic chaos as cars stall
items.description: Videos on social media showed cars stopped in the middle of multi-lane roads with their hazard lights on, obstructing traffic.
